correctness_confidence.basis: Checked: Lemma 1 (gap reduction) is sound, since a 3-AP of difference d<=N cannot cross a gap >N; the N=27 witness (18 elements in [0,54]) contains a 3-AP for every d<=27; the N=15 12-set of diameter 35 is valid. Theorem 1 gives m(16,3)=12, contradicting Table 1 (13). Z lower bounds for N=11..17 rest on unchecked CP-SAT status.

rigor.basis: Window DRUP proofs exist for k=3 with a homemade checker (not drat-trim). Z values for N=11..17 have no certificate, yet Theorem 1 states them as exact. Problem 27 lower bounds for p=29,31 are logged but not checked. My exhaustive search reproduces Table 3 for p<=19 (3,4,5,7,7,8,9).

novelty.basis: Authors disclaim priority for Problem 27 and say they found no earlier m(N,3) values. The literature search was limited (Green's list, Green-Ruzsa, two OEIS searches, a few web searches). I did not browse, so earlier values cannot be excluded. No new theorem found in the text.

significance.basis: Exact small-N values for a finite 3-AP covering problem. The paper admits no asymptotic content (section 5 item v) and makes no link to N^(1-c_k). The main content is computational at small scale.

reproducibility.basis: The supplement (code, witnesses, SHA-256 of proofs, Lean files) is referenced but was not in the reviewed artifact, so I could not inspect it. The N=27 witness is printed and checks. Section 4 states no theorem links the Lean checkers to the formal-conjectures statements.

summary: The manuscript reports exact or bounded values of m(N,3) for N<=17 and window-based upper bounds up to N=27, plus a reproduction of small Problem 27 values. The reduction in Lemma 1 is correct and the stated N=27 witness is valid. Theorem 1 contradicts its own Table 1 at N=16, and the exactness claims for N=11..17 rely on solver status without a certificate. The authors disclose that there is no human review and no formal verification. Recommendation: major revision.
strengths: Lemma 1 is a clean, correct normalization: a k-AP of difference d<=N cannot straddle a gap larger than N, so the gap-reduction preserves all required APs.
The N=27 witness (18 elements in [0,54]) contains a 3-AP for every d=1..27, as stated.
Problem 27 values for p<=19 are reproduced by my exhaustive search (3,4,5,7,7,8,9).
The window-vs-Z discrepancy at N=15 (12 in Z, 13 in the window) is stated openly and checks out via the explicit 12-set of diameter 35.
Section 5 and section 6 disclose limits honestly: no human review, no formal verification, no asymptotics, and a limited literature search.
weaknesses: Theorem 1 lists 18 values for N=1..17 (four 12s), while Table 1 and the text give three 12s and m(16,3)=13. The abstract repeats the same list.
For N=11..17, the Z lower bounds rest on CP-SAT status with no independent certificate, but Theorem 1 presents them as proved.
CaDiCaL was run only for N=13 in Z, so the solver cross-check covers one instance.
The RUP checker is homemade and is not drat-trim or a verified checker, and the paper trusts it.
No Lean statement connects the checkers to the formal-conjectures definitions, so the 'formal' component does not link to the stated problems.
The Problem 27 lower bounds for p=29 and 31 are logged but not checked, and the paper itself marks them as unchecked.
potential_errors: Theorem 1 and the abstract give m(16,3)=12, but Table 1 and the text (N=16 CP-SAT value equals the window value 13) give 13.
Theorem 1's list has 18 entries for N=1..17, so the list cannot be aligned with the N values without an extra or missing entry.
unresolved_material_objections: Main claim inconsistency: Theorem 1 (and the abstract) states m(16,3)=12, while Table 1 and the text give 13. Either the theorem or the table is wrong, and the exact value for N=16 is therefore not established as stated.

Exactness for N=11..17 in Z: Theorem 1 states m(N,3) as exact for these N, but the lower bounds rest on CP-SAT INFEASIBLE status with no independent certificate (section 4). Without a checked proof the claimed exact values are unsupported beyond solver output.
